questions.context:
When the old railway station in Branton closed in 1987, most people forgot about it. The tracks were removed, weeds grew between the stones, and the building slowly fell apart. Then, three years ago, a group of local teenagers had an unusual idea: let's turn it into a skate park.

Nobody believed it was possible. The council said the building was dangerous, and some older residents wanted it pulled down completely. But the teenagers refused to give up. They made a video showing their plan, collected over two thousand signatures, and presented their idea at a council meeting. 'We don't have anywhere to go after school,' said Mia Torres, one of the organisers. 'This could change everything.'

The council finally agreed to help — but only if the teenagers found the money themselves. So they organised concerts, sold cakes, and cleaned cars. Eighteen months later, they had enough.

Today, the Branton Skate Station welcomes around a hundred young people every day. It has ramps, a small café run by volunteers, and even a room for art classes. Mia, now at university, comes back every holiday. 'People told us we were dreaming,' she says. 'But sometimes dreams just need a bit of concrete.'
questions.stem: What happened to the station after it closed?
options: It became a skate park immediately.
It was forgotten and became ruined.
It was turned into a café.
questions.explanation: The tracks were removed, weeds grew, and the building fell apart.

tasks.title: Mock 4 · Part 1: Reply to Josh's email
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Josh. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
Sorry I haven't written for ages — I've been really busy with football training.
Listen, our team is coming to your town for a tournament next month, and we'll have a free Sunday! Do you know any good places to visit near the sports centre?
Also, I'd love to try some traditional food while I'm there. What should I eat?
And one more question — how do I get from the sports centre to the town centre? Is it far?
Hope to see you soon!
Josh
points: Suggest places to visit near the sports centre
Explain how to get to the town centre
Say if you can meet him
tasks.model:
Hi Josh,

Great to hear from you — and good luck in the tournament!

Near the sports centre, you should visit the river park. It's beautiful and perfect for relaxing after a match. There's also a small museum about the town's history.

For food, you must try our traditional meat pies — the best ones are at Miller's Bakery, just off the main square.

The town centre is only a fifteen-minute walk from the sports centre: go straight down King Street, and you're there.

I'd love to meet you on Sunday — phone me when you arrive!

Alex
tasks.modelNotes: Each point gets a clear answer; directions use imperatives; the closing arranges the meeting.
checklist: All four content points are answered
Suggestions and a recommendation are given

tasks.title: Mock 4 · Part 2: The message in the bottle
tasks.rubric: Your teacher has asked you to write a story with the title 'The message in the bottle'. Write your story (about 100 words).
points: End with a feeling or surprise
tasks.model:
The Message in the Bottle

Last summer, I was walking alone along the beach when I saw something green between the rocks. It was a bottle — and inside there was a piece of paper!

My hands were shaking as I opened it. The message said: 'If you find this bottle, meet me at the lighthouse at sunset. — E.'

Who was E? I thought about it all afternoon. In the end, curiosity won, and I went to the lighthouse.

An old man was waiting there, smiling. 'You found my bottle!' he said. 'I threw it into the sea forty years ago.' We talked until the stars appeared, and I learned the most amazing story of my life.

l_m4_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m4_p3_main.text: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to the Open Day at Westfield Community Garden. I'm Janet, and I started this garden eight years ago.

l_m4_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m4_p3_main.text: Westfield Garden is open every day from eight in the morning until eight in the evening. It covers about half of a hectare — small, but full of life. We grow more than thirty kinds of vegetables and fruit, from tomatoes to strawberries.

l_m4_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m4_p3_main.text: Anyone can join us. The membership costs twenty pounds a year, and members get their own small piece of land. We currently have seventy members, and there is space for ten more.

l_m4_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m4_p3_main.text: We also run free workshops every month. This month it's composting, next month beekeeping. Our most popular event is the harvest festival in September, when more than three hundred neighbours come to eat and celebrate together.

l_m4_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m4_p3_main.text: To join, just visit us during opening hours or email us at hello@westfieldgarden.org. Come and get your hands dirty!

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m4_p4_main.text: My guest today is sixteen-year-old Kai Nakamura, who cycles twenty kilometres to school every day — in Japan. Welcome, Kai.

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M2
l_m4_p4_main.text: Thank you! Yes, I live in the countryside, and my school is in the city. The journey takes about fifty minutes each way.

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m4_p4_main.text: Why do you cycle? Isn't there a bus?

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M2
l_m4_p4_main.text: There is a bus, but it's crowded and slow. My father suggested the bike when I was twelve. At first I hated it, especially in winter. But after a few months, I started to enjoy it. Now I can't imagine my mornings without it.

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m4_p4_main.text: What do you do with all that time on the road?

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M2
l_m4_p4_main.text: I listen to English podcasts — that's actually how I learned most of my English! I also think about my day, and sometimes I stop to take photos. The rice fields look amazing in autumn.

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m4_p4_main.text: Has cycling changed you in any way?

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M2
l_m4_p4_main.text: Definitely. I'm stronger, of course, but more importantly, I'm calmer. And my marks improved — my teachers say I concentrate better in the morning. Last year I even joined a junior cycling race and finished fifth!

l_m4_p4_main.speaker: M2
l_m4_p4_main.text: Good rain gear solves ninety percent of the problem! Only snow stops me — maybe five days a year. Then I take the bus, and I miss my bike immediately.
